en.summary: Heatwave risk is {level} for {city} on {date} ({probability:.0%} probability).
en.disclaimer: This is an automated research-model alert, not an official warning. Please follow IMD and local authority advisories.

MODERATE: Carry a water bottle and sip water regularly, even if you don't feel thirsty.
Apply sunscreen (SPF 30+) before going out and reapply every 2-3 hours.
Wear light-colored, loose cotton clothes and a cap or scarf.
HIGH: Carry a water bottle and sip water regularly, even if you don't feel thirsty.
Apply sunscreen (SPF 30+) before going out and reapply every 2-3 hours.
Wear light-colored, loose cotton clothes and a cap or scarf.
Avoid going out between 12 pm and 4 pm if you can.
Carry ORS or lemon water/buttermilk, and take breaks in the shade.
Check on elderly relatives, young children and neighbors living alone.
Never leave children or pets in a parked vehicle.
EXTREME: Carry a water bottle and sip water regularly, even if you don't feel thirsty.
Apply sunscreen (SPF 30+) before going out and reapply every 2-3 hours.
Wear light-colored, loose cotton clothes and a cap or scarf.
Avoid going out between 12 pm and 4 pm if you can.
Carry ORS or lemon water/buttermilk, and take breaks in the shade.
Check on elderly relatives, young children and neighbors living alone.
Never leave children or pets in a parked vehicle.
Stay indoors during the hottest hours and postpone strenuous outdoor work or exercise.

Know the signs of heatstroke: very high body temperature, confusion, dizziness, nausea, hot dry skin or fainting. This is an emergency: move the person to a cool place, cool them down with water, and call emergency services (108 or 112 in India).
Outdoor workers: take frequent shade breaks and follow your employer's and local authorities' heat guidance.
